text:
Nora (Design): Quick review: new threshold control proposal. Two toggles: 'Absolute' (e.g., 5 errors) and 'Relative' (e.g., 2% of requests). Wire: https://figma.redwood/threshold-toggle. Need feedback on copy and SLO implications.

Hector (Eng): Implementation wise relative thresholds need baseline window (e.g., last 24h) to compute % — we should surface that selection. Also perf note: don’t compute live on every keystroke for heavy queries.

Priya (Product): UX note: users confuse % vs ratio. Suggest label "Relative (percent of traffic)" and show a small helper: "Compared to baseline window: last 1h / 24h / 7d".

Maya (PM): Also multi-tenant teams care about which baseline to use. Add a small dropdown: Baseline window — default 24h. Keep default copy: "Compare to most recent 24 hours."

Jon (A11y): Screen reader announcement: when user toggles between Absolute/Relative, announce the selected mode and the currently selected baseline. Example: "Threshold mode: Relative. Baseline: 24 hours." Use aria-live=polite.

Nora (Design): Good call. I'll add an aria-live region tied to the mode control. UX question: do we hide the baseline dropdown when Absolute is selected?

Hector (Eng): Hide it visually but keep it in the DOM with aria-hidden toggled off for SRs when visible. Avoid rendering/unmounting to prevent state loss.

Priya (Product): Another copy concern: threshold preview line currently reads "Will notify when > 2%" — better: "Notify when error rate > 2% over baseline". More explicit.

Liam (Analytics): For clarity show expected sample size for Relative mode: e.g., "2% (based on ~12k requests in last 24h)". Helps trust in small-volume services.

Nora (Design): I'll add the sample-size annotation under the preview. On mobile we collapse it under a "details" chevron. Any accessibility concerns?

Jon (A11y): Ensure collapsed region has an accessible summary and `aria-expanded` on the button. The collapsed content should be focusable and read by SR when expanded.

Maya (PM): Suppression windows: request to support recurring schedules (e.g., weekdays 09:00-17:00). Wire has a simple "one-off" selector — can we extend to recurrence?

Hector (Eng): Recurrence is doable but increases complexity. Recommend MVP: presets (business hours, weekend) + custom recurrence modal (cron-like) for advanced users. Keep plain text summary: "Suppression: Weekdays 09:00-17:00 (UTC)".

Priya (Product): Timezone copy: default to user's timezone but allow explicit timezone selection. UI should show timezone tag so teams know what timeframe is applied.

i18n-bot: Reminder: when showing timezone names, use localized formats. E.g., en-US: "9:00 AM - 5:00 PM (GMT+1)".

Nora (Design): Copy decision: use "Suppression" as label, helptext: "Temporarily pause notifications for selected channels. Recurring schedules available."

Jon (A11y): For SRs say: "Suppression active: Weekdays 09:00-17:00 in Europe/Paris. Notifications will be paused." Keep phrasing short.

Liam (Analytics): Small ask: expose next three suppression occurrences in preview so users can verify recurrence. E.g., "Next occurrences: Mon 03/21 09:00, Tue 03/22 09:00, Wed 03/23 09:00". Should be generated server-side.

Hector (Eng): Agree. We'll add an endpoint to compute occurrences. Rate-limit the preview calls.

Nora (Design): Final layout decision: preview header shows mode (Absolute/Relative), threshold value, baseline (if relative), sample size, and suppression summary badge. I'll update figma and include aria-live text samples. Target: prototype by Wednesday.

Priya (Product): Thanks — will validate with a few customer use cases. If anyone wants to pair on the recurrence UX, ping me.

Maya (PM): I'll add a checklist item for QA: timezone edge-cases, SR announcements, collapsed mobile detail.

Jon (A11y): Happy to review the ARIA markup before QA.

Nora (Design): Thanks all!
